newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares seek to maintain hefty gains.
newsitem.headline: German shares seek to maintain hefty gains.

text.p: German shares sought in post-bourse IBIS computer dealings on Tuesday to hold onto hefty gains after the DAX index closed bourse trade above 4,000 points for the first time in history.
The IBIS DAX was up 12.86 points at 4,016.21 points, which was above the bourse close at 4,006.40 points.
Traders said the opening of Wall Street may trigger profit-taking in the German market ahead of the day's close.
"There's a good chance for some profit-taking and the DAX may dip below 4,000 points," said one trader. "But we should end the day just under 4,000 or even a bit higher."
The share market forged ahead in bourse dealings on Tuesday as the firm dollar lifted the blue chip DAX index to its sixth record close in a row.
Prices had initially weakened on profit taking in the pre-bourse session, but dealers said the market had just drawn breath during a giddy ascent and was still in bullish form.
"We are still looking at a solid uptrend," said one dealer. "The dollar puts everything else, including Wall Street in the shade."
Nineteen of the DAX-30 stocks advanced while 11 fell.

Electronics and engineering group Siemens AG hit an all-time high of 110.10 marks during the session amid talk of changes in its GPT telecoms joint venture but interest waned and the share ended at 108.75 marks, up just 10 pfennigs.
Siemens said there would be no change in ownership of GPT.
Other key gainers included Metro AG, the retailer whose shares surged on Monday after it said it was mulling buying the cash and carry business of Dutch retailer SHV Holdings.
Metro, whose annual general meeting is set for Wednesday, gained 10.90 marks to end the bourse at 216.40 marks.
Carmakers, which are sensitive to the dollar, were higher.

BMW AG came into focus after the British press said it might sell its Rover small car unit to Chrysler Corp but the German carmaker dismissed the report as nonsense. Its shares ended the bourse session up 24 marks at 1,491 marks.
Volkswagen AG rose 56 marks to 1,491 marks.

The German unemployment report for June had moderate impact on the market. Dealers said there was no reaction from the headline figures, which showed a seasonally adjusted 11,000 rise in June from May, but said the trend indicated that there was little risk of a rise in German interest rates.
